run.question: Show me the logs and resource recommendations for the pod api-gateway in namespace app-102a

report.summary:
The pod asked about exists and is running: app-102a/api-gateway-585c5579f6-2pwgm, a single nginx container (image nginx:latest) on node opspilot-m1-control-plane, Ready with restartCount 0 at the time of query (19:00:18Z). It is owned by ReplicaSet api-gateway-585c5579f6, which is owned by Deployment api-gateway (1/1 ready, Available and Progressing True); events show the deployment-controller scaling that ReplicaSet from 0 to 1 at 19:00:07Z and the kubelet scheduling/pulling/starting the container by 19:00:08Z, i.e. the pod object is seconds old and no crash, OOMKill, eviction or probe failure event appears anywhere in the window's events.

Logs: the kubelet stream holds 23 lines, all nginx startup output ending in "Configuration complete; ready for start up" (nginx/1.31.9, worker processes started), with no error text; there is no previous container instance. Loki holds 37 lines for pod=api-gateway-585c5579f6-2pwgm between 18:00:08Z and 19:00:08Z, all level INFO "HTTP request completed" GETs (/health, /api/v1/orders, /api/v1/users, /api/v1/inventory, /api/v1/products) with statuses 200/201/204 and response_time_ms 50-195; the last-hour status breakdown is 200:27, 201:3, 204:6 and no 4xx/5xx series was returned. So in the log evidence examined, this pod's own requests show no error-level lines or error status codes.

Resource recommendations (advisory): the container declares no CPU or memory requests or limits at all and the pod is QoS class BestEffort; it also has no readinessProbe/livenessProbe, no HPA and no ResourceQuota in the namespace, and no Service exists in app-102a. I could not verify actual CPU/memory consumption to size requests, because every Prometheus query in this Run failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and Jaeger was unavailable as well; the numbers below are therefore recommendations, not measured conclusions.

claims.text: Pod app-102a/api-gateway-585c5579f6-2pwgm is phase Running on node opspilot-m1-control-plane with QoS class BestEffort, container nginx Ready=True, restartCount 0 and no previous container instance, observed at 2026-11-23T19:00:18Z.

The container (and the Deployment api-gateway pod template) declares image nginx:latest, an empty resources object (no requests.cpu, requests.memory, limits.cpu or limits.memory) and no readinessProbe or livenessProbe; strategy is RollingUpdate and deployment generation is 1.

Ownership chain is complete: ReplicaSet api-gateway-585c5579f6 (created 2026-11-23T19:00:07Z, 1 replica ready) is owned by Deployment api-gateway, which reports 1/1 replicas ready and available and conditions Available=True, Progressing=True.

All 11 events in the authorized window include: Deployment api-gateway ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set api-gateway-585c5579f6 from 0 to 1' at 19:00:07Z, ReplicaSet api-gateway-585c5579f6 SuccessfulCreate 'Created pod: api-gateway-585c5579f6-2pwgm', and kubelet Normal events Scheduled, Pulling, Pulled, Created and Started between 19:00:07Z and 19:00:08Z; no OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff or Unhealthy reason appears for this pod.

Kubelet logs for container nginx contain 23 lines from 2026-11-23T19:00:08.293Z to 19:00:08.329Z, all nginx startup output ('Configuration complete; ready for start up', nginx/1.31.9, worker processes 36-43 started) with no error or warning text; no previous container instance exists, so there are no logs from an earlier container.

Loki lines for labels pod=api-gateway-585c5579f6-2pwgm, namespace=app-102a, app=nginx, job=nginx, service_name=nginx number 37 between 18:00:08Z and 19:00:08Z, every one level INFO 'HTTP request completed' GET with status 200, 201 or 204, on paths /health, /api/v1/orders, /api/v1/users, /api/v1/inventory and /api/v1/products, with response_time_ms values between 50 and 195.
In the hour 18:00:15Z-19:00:15Z Loki counts by status are 200: 27 lines, 201: 3 lines, 204: 6 lines (36 lines total); no series for any 4xx or 5xx status was returned.
A 7-day Loki count_over_time grouped by detected_level for this pod returns a single series, detected_level=info, with 100 lines, i.e. no line with another detected_level is counted in that view.
Namespace app-102a contains no Service, no HorizontalPodAutoscaler and no ResourceQuota at query time.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports allocatable 8 CPU, 32859952Ki memory and 110 pods, and across the cluster only kube-system/coredns, kube-system/metrics-server, otel-demo/kube-state-metrics and otel-demo/prometheus-readonly-proxy declare CPU requests, while most otel-demo deployments declare only memory limits - api-gateway declares neither.

The only Warning events in the window are four FailedToCreateEndpoint events for Services loki (namespaces app-100a, app-101, app-102) and mariadb (app-219) in the default event namespace ('endpoints "loki"/"mariadb" already exists'); none of them names an object in app-102a or api-gateway.

Add explicit CPU and memory requests and limits to the nginx container of Deployment api-gateway (currently QoS BestEffort with an empty resources block). Because no usage series could be read in this Run (Prometheus unreachable), measure container CPU/memory first and set requests from observed steady-state usage with limits above it, rather than copying arbitrary numbers; the node has 8 CPU and ~32Gi allocatable, so capacity is not the constraint.

Add a readinessProbe and a livenessProbe to the nginx container - the logs show /health answering 200, so an HTTP GET /health on port 80 is available - so that traffic and restarts react to a hung gateway; today no probe of either kind is defined.

Pin the image instead of nginx:latest (the running build reports nginx/1.31.9) so restarts and rollouts are reproducible, and create a Service for the pod if it is intended to serve cluster traffic - namespace app-102a currently contains no Service, so nothing selects this pod today.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query (kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="app-102a"}) and get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no container CPU/memory usage series or node utilization was obtained and the sizing numbers cannot be verified against measured consumption.
Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace/span evidence exists for the pod's requests; the listed trace service names did not include api-gateway or nginx.

A Loki line filter for error|warn|fail|exception|panic|timeout|refused over the authorized window returned no rows with status no_data; an empty match is not proof that no error line exists, so absence of error-level log lines is unproven beyond the INFO lines actually returned.

Loki line counts are internally inconsistent: 36 lines counted in the hour 18:00:15Z-19:00:15Z versus 100 lines counted over the 7 days 2026-11-16T19:00:15Z-2026-11-23T19:00:15Z; Loki retention/ingest completeness and any volume or rate trend are therefore unknown.

The Loki lines are labelled pod=api-gateway-585c5579f6-2pwgm but carry timestamps from 18:00:08Z, before that pod object was created at 19:00:07Z, so I could not verify that they belong to this pod instance rather than an earlier one with the same name.

Kubelet retains only 23 startup lines (pod was ~8 seconds old when queried) and has no previous container instance, so the pod's runtime behaviour during the rest of the authorized window could not be read from the kubelet log stream.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so who created or last modified Deployment api-gateway (and whether a change triggered the 0-to-1 scale-up at 19:00:07Z) could not be determined.
LimitRange objects are not in the readable kind list for this environment, so namespace-level default resource limits (which could explain an empty resources block) could not be checked.
next_steps: Restore or point the Run at a reachable Prometheus and read container_cpu_usage_seconds_total / container_memory_working_set_bytes for pod api-gateway-585c5579f6-2pwgm to derive concrete request and limit values.
Review Loki with a longer retention query for pod=~"api-gateway.*" in app-102a to reconcile the 36-lines-per-hour versus 100-lines-per-7-days discrepancy and to confirm the level distribution.

Confirm with the cluster owner whether api-gateway in app-102a is intended to be exposed by a Service and whether a LimitRange or policy requires resource requests; there is currently no Service, no HPA and no ResourceQuota in that namespace.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
